clue.text: Low cloud allowed silence to envelop river bird

indicators.note: to envelop is to wrap round, so the word for silence goes around the river

blocks.note: mist is cloud lying low on the ground
let means allowed
hush is silence
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Mist that hushes everything wraps around a river where a bird is perched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low cloud' is one idea, ground-level mist; 'allowed' and 'silence' are separate pieces, with the river abbreviation tucked inside the word for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistle thrush is a large European songbird that feeds on mistletoe berries.

clue.text: Graduate reduced means of catching animal disease

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the final letter of the catching device is dropped

blocks.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate
a lariat is a lasso used to catch cattle

explanation.surface: A graduate's reduced way of catching an animal disease, as though studying vets' methods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal' looks part of the disease, but it belongs with the lasso: a lariat catches animals. Drop its last letter after MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaria is a mosquito-borne fever caused by a parasite, a classic tropical disease.

clue.text: Pan group concealing murder

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something inside, so the word for group holds the other word

blocks.note: a set is a group
to kill is to murder

explanation.surface: A gang covers up a killing — 'pan' reads like a verb for criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: A skillet is a frying pan, a long-handled cooking vessel.

clue.text: Provides checks for each non-expert

indicators.note: checks means holds in or restrains, so the phrase for provides holds the other word

blocks.note: lays on means provides, as in laying on a meal
per means for each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: Someone supplies cheques for each person who is no expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checks' looks like inspects or cheques; it means restrains, holding the Latin 'for each' inside a two-word phrase for provides.
explanation.definitionFit: A layperson is someone without professional or specialist knowledge of a subject.

clue.text: Stories become hackneyed when lead character appears last

indicators.note: the first letter moving round to the end rotates the word by one place

blocks.note: something hackneyed has gone stale

explanation.surface: Stories get tired and predictable when the hero only shows up at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Become hackneyed' gives STALE; its S moves from the front to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Tales are narratives or stories, real or invented.

clue.text: Valued customer according to standard practice

blocks.note: first meaning: a frequent, loyal patron
second meaning: normal, conforming to the usual rule

explanation.surface: A shop treats its prized customer by the book.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a habitual patron of a pub or shop and an adjective for normal or conventional.

clue.text: Foreign place is distinctive

indicators.note: foreign suggests something made strange and unfamiliar, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An abroad location stands out as unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is 'place is', so 'is' does double duty here as letters rather than a link; the definition is 'distinctive'.
explanation.definitionFit: Special means out of the ordinary, marked off from others — distinctive.

clue.text: Unsuitable, popular program likely to entertain Conservative

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so the word for likely holds the party letter

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
an app is a software program
liable to means likely to
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A trendy TV show that invites a Tory guest is judged inappropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Program' with its American spelling is the computing sense, a piece of software on a phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapplicable means not relevant or appropriate to the case, hence unsuitable.

clue.text: Quash flawed conclusion of treaty in full

indicators.note: something flawed is faulty, so these letters are in the wrong order
the conclusion of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: the final letter of treaty
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lawyer moves to overturn a faulty ending in a treaty's full text.
explanation.definitionFit: To nullify is to make legally void, which is what quashing a verdict or order does.

clue.text: Drunk for example sells off clothes

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters are disordered
clothes is a verb here: to dress is to cover around, so the rearranged letters wrap the abbreviation

blocks.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk, say, flogs his clothes for drink money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off clothes' reads as undressing, but 'off' signals the shuffle and 'clothes' is a verb for wrapping round. Legless is British slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Legless is British slang for so intoxicated one cannot stand up.

clue.text: Loose piglets startled caveman?

indicators.note: startled animals scatter in every direction, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Escaped piglets frighten a prehistoric man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caveman' suggests a Stone Age figure; the question mark flags a whimsical reading as a man who studies caves.
explanation.definitionFit: A speleologist studies or explores caves, so is a 'cave man' in a playful literal sense.

clue.text: One penned no more, leaving sentence unfinished

blocks.note: first meaning: a person no longer shut up in prison
second meaning: someone let out before their prison term has run its course

explanation.surface: A writer gives up mid-sentence, penning nothing further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' and 'sentence' point to writing; both belong to prison, where a pen is an enclosure and a sentence is a term served.
explanation.definitionFit: A parolee is a prisoner released early under supervision, free before the full term is served.

clue.text: Heraldic device's alternate elements in small flag

indicators.note: alternate elements are every other letter, taking the first, third and fifth

blocks.note: the odd letters of small
to flag is to tire, grow weary

explanation.surface: A coat of arms is set with alternating parts of a little banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner beside 'heraldic', but it is the verb meaning to weaken; 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal cross on a shield or flag, an ordinary in heraldry, as on Scotland's flag.

clue.text: Did list compile antisocial cases?

indicators.note: cases as a verb means encloses, so the two words hold the answer within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Did someone draw up a list of antisocial behaviour cases?
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' reads as a noun for compiling; here it is the verb to lean over, as a ship lists.
explanation.definitionFit: To list is to tilt to one side, so a ship that listed leant over.

clue.text: What can be used to fix plug and re-use fitting?

definitions.text: What can be used to fix

indicators.note: fitting means putting parts together into a new arrangement, so the letters are assembled afresh

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: A DIY question about what mends a broken plug fitting so it can be used again.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as the answer: strong glue fixes a plug fitting for re-use.
explanation.definitionFit: Superglue is a fast-setting adhesive used to stick or mend things firmly.

clue.text: Depression hit British member of parliament

blocks.note: to punch is to hit
B is the abbreviation for British
a group of owls is called a parliament

explanation.surface: A British MP is struck by a bout of depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member of parliament' wants to be an MP; it is a bird, since a parliament is the collective noun for owls.
explanation.definitionFit: A punchbowl is a bowl-shaped hollow in hills, a geographical depression, such as the Devil's Punch Bowl in Surrey.

clue.text: Tin containing new filling: potato and cabbage

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the word for tin holds the abbreviation
filling means going inside, so the combined chunk sits within the punctuation mark that follows

blocks.note: a can is a tin
N is the abbreviation for new
the punctuation mark itself is named

explanation.surface: A can holding a fresh filling of mashed potato and cabbage.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon in the clue is part of the wordplay: CA(N)N goes inside COLON. 'Filling' looks like food in the can.
explanation.definitionFit: Colcannon is an Irish dish of mashed potatoes mixed with cabbage or kale.

clue.text: Unloading vessel carrying less weight

blocks.note: first meaning: a flat barge used to unload ships
second meaning: less heavy

explanation.surface: A ship being unloaded rides higher with less cargo aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a barge that ferries goods from a ship to shore, and lighter is also the comparative of light.

clue.text: Flap about supporting one who bemoans losing wife

indicators.note: losing means giving up, so one letter is removed from the mourner
in a down clue supporting means sitting underneath, so this piece comes after the other

blocks.note: on means about, concerning
a wailer is someone who laments
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A widower in a flap after losing his wife, propped up by friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flap' looks like a state of panic; it is the hinged control surface. WAILER loses W, then ON goes below it.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is a hinged flap on an aircraft wing that controls roll.

clue.text: Summer's end is complete

blocks.note: first meaning: what someone who adds figures ends up with
second meaning: absolute, utter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' is not the season but one who sums; the end of their work is the sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is the final sum of an addition, and total as an adjective means complete or absolute.

clue.text: Effective narration

blocks.note: first meaning: having a striking, revealing impact
second meaning: the act of relating a story

explanation.walkthrough: Two separate meanings of one word, one adjective and one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A telling remark is one with a strong, revealing effect, and the telling of a tale is its narration.

clue.text: Little outing possibly for group in bar

blocks.note: a trip is an outing
-let is a suffix meaning small, as in piglet

explanation.surface: A short trip out, perhaps for a group having a drink in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub; it is a bar of music. 'Possibly' marks the definition as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a triplet is a group of three notes played in the time of two, found within a bar.

clue.text: Is taken aback by plastic leg found in toilets

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable into any shape, so these letters are reshaped
found in means placed inside, so the remoulded letters sit within the toilets

blocks.note: taken as written
bog is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked to find a prosthetic leg left in the public toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: Bog is British slang for a toilet. The definition reads as 'boggles at' with 'by' in place of 'at'.
explanation.definitionFit: If your mind boggles at something, you are astonished or taken aback by it.

clue.text: Upset after Liberal's heightened division

indicators.note: the Liberal is raised, and in a down entry raised means moved up the column, so that one letter shifts to an earlier spot

blocks.note: spilt means upset, as a knocked-over drink

explanation.surface: A political party is upset after its Liberal wing grows more prominent and splits away.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the abbreviation for Liberal, and 's stands for 'is': in SPILT the L moves one place higher in the down entry, ahead of the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A split is a division, especially a break within a group or party.

clue.text: Supply of food providing assistance

blocks.note: first meaning: a portion served at a meal
second meaning: giving aid

explanation.surface: A food bank hands out supplies, offering aid to those in need.
explanation.definitionFit: A helping is a serving of food, and helping is also the present participle of help, to assist.

clue.text: Log almost everything to do with food processing facilities

definitions.text: to do with food processing facilities

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

blocks.note: to log data is to enter it
all means everything

explanation.surface: A record is kept of nearly everything about a factory's food processing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food processing facilities' suggests factories; it is the gut, which processes food.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteral means relating to the intestines, the body's own food-processing organs.

clue.text: Fancy ladies room expels raving mad, flighty creatures

indicators.note: expels means throws out, so certain letters are removed
fancy means elaborate or ornamental, so the remaining letters are dressed up in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
raving mad simply means mad

explanation.surface: A posh ladies' room throws out some wild and flighty women.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of MAD from LADIES ROOM, then rearrange what is left. 'Flighty' looks like fickle; it is literal, as in able to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Orioles are brightly coloured songbirds, creatures that take flight.

clue.text: Reveal cartel originally took over to stop corruption

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the first letter of the following word is used
to stop a gap is to plug it, so the combined chunk goes inside the word for corruption

blocks.note: a ring is a group colluding to fix prices
the first letter of took
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
blight is decay or corruption

explanation.surface: A cartel's dealings are first exposed when someone steps in to halt the corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cartel' suggests drugs, but here it is a price-fixing ring; the three short pieces sit inside the word for corruption after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring to light is to make known something hidden, i.e. to reveal or disclose it.
